title: Residency routing & log handoff constraints — Banyan Capital intake
summary: Initial compliance/residency discovery to determine whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private is feasible for Banyan's EU + US regulated workloads. Key concerns: EU data residency, audit/log redaction, KMS residency, operator access, and fallback behavior across regions.
topics: Data residency (EU vs US) and cross-border access
Persistent logs vs ephemeral telemetry and redaction
KMS/HSM key residency and customer-managed keys
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Operator access, canary/fallback policies, and SLO implications
action_items: Maya Chen: Send SOC 2 + ISO27001 evidence pack and HIPAA summary (due 2027-03-04)
Rafael Ortiz: Draft VPC/private deployment diagram showing region-locking, peering, and how KV cache / prefix caching is handled (due 2027-03-10)
Evan Hart (Banyan): Share sample log payloads and list of PII fields we must redact before sending to any hosted service (due 2027-03-05)
Maya Chen: Provide ballpark pricing for Dedicated 2-region reserved capacity and private deployment estimate (due 2027-03-05)
Marcus Liu (Banyan): Confirm compliance reviewers' availability for a technical deep dive next week (due 2027-03-07)
next_steps: Schedule SE deep dive for private deployment feasibility (Redwood + Banyan infra + compliance)
Redwood to circulate security evidence and deployment diagram
Customer to produce short data flow & retention requirements doc before pilot scoping
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (scheduled 45)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Alisha Rao (Banyan Head of Data), Marcus Liu (CTO), Priya Kapoor (Compliance), Evan Hart (Infra)

Summary: quick intake to understand residency constraints and logging restrictions; explore Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and what evidence Banyan needs for internal auditors.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh — appreciate you taking the time. Quick intro from our side, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Rafael's our SE.
[00:08] Alisha Rao: Hi all, Alisha here. We'll keep it focused — we have folks from infra and compliance on.
[00:12] Marcus Liu: Marcus, CTO. Short on time so we wanna figure out whether we can do hosted or need private.
[00:19] Rafael Ortiz: Great. High level, we'll walk through how Redwood routes requests, what logs we retain, and options for Dedicated/Private with customer-managed KMS and region locking.
[00:27] Priya Kapoor: Thanks. Our big blockers: GDPR — data residency in EU, HIPAA-ish for a small subset of data in US, and auditors want proof that logs with PII never leave EU datacenters.
[00:39] Evan Hart: Also operator access — we need to know who at Redwood can access data, for support, and whether that's logged.
[00:45] Rafael Ortiz: Sure. Quick clarification — when you say "logs with PII," do you mean raw user inputs, or meta logs? We often separate transcript logs (token traces) from service-level telemetry.
[00:55] Priya Kapoor: Raw user inputs — e.g., customer documents — must not leave EU. Telemetry like latency/error rates is ok but anonymized.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Right, that maps to our typical distinctions. For Hosted — our EU region keeps data in EU for customers that select EU tenancy, but some backup/failover paths can cross region unless you choose Dedicated or Private with region locking.
[01:18] Marcus Liu: Can you define "some backup pathways"? Our counsel will reject any cross-border replication without explicit contract-level guarantees.
[01:25] Rafael Ortiz: Under Hosted default, we replicate minimal metadata across regions for control-plane availability. For strict residency you want Dedicated with region affinity or Private where control plane is customer-managed and you can avoid cross-border replication.
[01:38] Alisha Rao: So Dedicated guarantees compute stays in selected region? And logs?
[01:42] Rafael Ortiz: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in region and data residency guarantees per SLA — logs for inference can be configured to be retained only in-region and to be forwarded to your VPC or S3 in-region.
[01:53] Evan Hart: Can we push logs directly into our S3 in AWS eu-west-1? We want them land in our bucket first, so Redwood never stores raw inputs.
[02:01] Rafael Ortiz: Yes — for Dedicated/Private we support VPC egress to your endpoint; you can route request payloads to your sink first or have Redwood store ephemeral data that is then pushed to your bucket and auto-deleted. There's also an option for customer-managed KMS so keys are in your tenancy.
[02:16] Priya Kapoor: KMS is critical. We need to know key residency and whether Redwood operators can decrypt logs.
[02:22] Maya Chen: You can use customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) in Dedicated or Private. That means Redwood can't decrypt without an API call that you can control and audit. For Hosted with BYOK there are caveats — some control-plane metadata still flows through Redwood.
[02:36] Marcus Liu: About operator access — what's your incident support model? Will support staff ever spin up a debug session with customer data accessible?
[02:44] Rafael Ortiz: Operator access is role-based. For Dedicated and Private we provide granular RBAC and most access is via support playbooks that require privileged request approvals. All actions are logged to audit trails; we can provide those logs for audits.
[02:56] Alisha Rao: Those audit trails — are they retained in-region? And can they be redacted before release to us?
[03:02] Rafael Ortiz: Audit trails for Dedicated can be stored in your VPC/S3 so they stay in-region. Redaction is something we can run as a post-process; we can also push raw logs into your bucket and you run your own redactor.
[03:14] Marcus Liu: What's your policy on transcript retention? Our compliance wants default short retention and ability to opt-out of retaining original prompts.
[03:21] Maya Chen: We have configurable retention windows per tenant. For Hosted default it's 30 days for raw prompts, but for regulated customers you can set to 0 (i.e., don't retain) and use streaming-only or pushing to customer sink. Dedicated and Private allow more control.
[03:34] Evan Hart: If we set retention to 0 and push to our S3, will Redwood still have any caches like KV or prefix cache that would contain user-derived data?
[03:42] Rafael Ortiz: Good question. The runtime uses KV cache for generation performance. For sensitive payloads you can disable caching or have the cache stored ephemeral in-region and wiped per-policy. For Private deployments you control the cache lifecycle. There's some nuance with continuous batching — that aggregates tokens but doesn't persist raw inputs beyond the configured window.
[04:02] Priya Kapoor: I heard "K V cache" in another call transcribed as something else — can you explain the risk briefly?
[04:07] Rafael Ortiz: Yeah, sorry — KV cache holds model key-value states for in-flight sessions. It can contain transient token context. If you absolutely cannot have any residual context, the SE recommends disabling prefix/KV caching or running in Private with guaranteed wipe on session end.
[04:22] Alisha Rao: Are there examples of customers who run entirely within EU and got auditor signoff?
[04:26] Maya Chen: Yes — several financial customers run Dedicated in eu-west with BYOK and tenant isolation — auditors accepted that. We can share redacted reference letters.
[04:35] Marcus Liu: What about fallbacks? Suppose eu-west capacity drops and there's a routing fallback to us-east. How's that handled contractually?
[04:42] Rafael Ortiz: By default routing policies prefer region but can have tiered fallbacks. For regulated customers we implement region-lock policies that block cross-region failover; that can impact availability SLOs. We can document tradeoffs.
[04:55] Evan Hart: That could be a dealbreaker if latency suffers during incidents. We'll need to balance.
[04:59] Maya Chen: Right, this is a classic latency vs residency tradeoff. We'll capture what service levels you need, and whether isolation is non-negotiable.
[05:07] Priya Kapoor: For audits we need evidence of encryption at rest/in transit, key handling, staff access controls, and log retention proofs. Can Redwood produce those artifacts?
[05:15] Rafael Ortiz: Totally. We'll share certs (SOC 2, ISO), our KMS integration docs, audit log formats, and a runbook for incident access.
[05:24] Alisha Rao: Also need legal language — model hallucination liabilities, cross-border clauses. Who owns what on data processing?
[05:31] Maya Chen: We'll loop legal, but generally data processing terms are in the DPA — we can flag the cross-border terms and residency clauses.
[05:37] Marcus Liu: On implementation: If we want a pilot, what's the minimum setup? We need to prove logs never leave EU and that operator access is auditable.
[05:46] Rafael Ortiz: Minimum pilot: Dedicated region with VPC egress to your S3 in eu-west-1, BYOK, and retention set to zero on Redwood side. We'll run sample workloads and you validate logs. That needs small reserved capacity and SE time for setup.
[05:57] Evan Hart: Timeline? We want to show this to auditors in ~3 weeks. Can you meet that?
[06:01] Maya Chen: We can aim for a pilot kickoff within two weeks if the feasibility deep dive goes well. Rafael, can we do a SE deep dive early next week?
[06:10] Rafael Ortiz: Yep — I'll prepare architecture and what changes are needed to runtime caching in Private mode.
[06:16] Alisha Rao: A couple quick clarifying items — do you ever store PII in backups? Backups must be EU-located.
[06:23] Rafael Ortiz: For Dedicated we can keep backups in-region; for Hosted defaults backups may be geo-redundant unless you opt into region-lock. For Private we leave backups to customer's ops.
[06:33] Priya Kapoor: On retention proofs — can you produce a short report showing deletion timestamps after we run the pilot?
[06:39] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, we can produce a retention/deletion audit log for the pilot run.
[06:44] Marcus Liu: About eDiscovery/legal hold — if legal hold is invoked, how does that interact with retention windows?
[06:51] Maya Chen: Legal hold can be applied to a tenant and will override deletion for the scope you define. That can be bounded by request. We'll need legal to coordinate.
[06:59] Evan Hart: Any known limitations with quantized models and Private installs? We use smaller models in latency-sensitive flows.
[07:06] Rafael Ortiz: Quantization works in our runtime; in Private we can ship quantized kernels and optimize for the hardware you run. We need to check specific model compatibility.
[07:15] Alisha Rao: Great. Let's talk about what we expect Redwood to send after this call.
[07:19] Maya Chen: We'll send: SOC2/ISO evidence, HIPAA summary, a VPC/private deployment diagram, and ballpark pricing for Dedicated 2-region commit.
[07:27] Priya Kapoor: We'll send sample logs and compliance checklist.
[07:30] Maya Chen: Cool. Rafael, anything else?
[07:33] Rafael Ortiz: I'll add a short note on disabling KV/prefix caching and implications for latency. Also include the audit-log format and how to wire it to your S3.
[07:43] Marcus Liu: Ok, that's fine. If we get the artifacts and the SE deep dive looks good we'll plan pilot.
[07:48] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with next steps and DPA pointers.
[07:52] Alisha Rao: Thanks.

End of transcript.
